svg.title: A nurse is reviewing fall risk factors for an older adult client admitted to a medical unit. Which of the following are EXTRINSIC fall risk factors? (Select all that apply.)
svg.desc: EXTRINSIC RISK FACTORS ARE IN THE ENVIRONMENT: clutter, an out-of-reach call light, improper footwear, wet floors, poor lighting, cords, and a bed left in a high position. INTRINSIC factors belong to the client, including advanced age, a history of falls, weakness, confusion, sensory deficits, incontinence, orthostatic hypotension, and medications such as diuretics, sedatives, and antihypertensives. Therefore the furosemide and lorazepam use and the fall history are intrinsic, not extrinsic.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Fall Prevention
Read the situation
A nurse is reviewing fall risk factors for
an older adult client admitted to a
medical unit. Which of the following are
EXTRINSIC fall risk factors? (Select all
that apply.)
What fits here
A cluttered pathway between the bed and
the bathroom · The call light is placed on
a table out of the client's reach · The
client ambulates in loose slippers with
smooth soles
Why it fits
EXTRINSIC RISK FACTORS ARE IN THE
ENVIRONMENT: clutter, an out-of-reach call
light, improper footwear, wet floors, poor
lighting, cords, and a bed left in a high
position.
